boxes.label: Theorem C35
boxes.statement: Any finite triangle-free simple graph with no independent set of size 10 that contains an induced copy of the circulant C35(1,7,11,16) (vertices 0..34, u ~ v iff v − u ≡ ±1, ±7, ±11 or ±16 mod 35) has at most 39 vertices, and any four distinct vertices outside the copy induce a 4-cycle.
boxes.also: So no triangle-free graph on 40 vertices with no independent 10-set contains an induced C35(1,7,11,16).
boxes.posed: The question was posed in public before: by Unsolved Lab (M20, 1 Oct, not run), in the repository andrey-kokoev/marici (a note dated 9 Nov: “this extension family has not been excluded”) and by an idea scout of Chen’s run (21 Nov, timed out). Nobody had decided it.

corollary.text: In a triangle-free graph on 40 vertices with no independent set of size 10, deleting any 5 vertices leaves an independent set of size 9; so at least 6 deletions are needed to leave none.
corollary.label: prose proof, not in Lean, conditional on Goedgebeur–Radziszowski’s uniqueness of the (3,9;35)-graph; derived in a reading by GPT-6.2-astra (a control-room session) and checked by the control room

boxes.why39: Call the copy’s 35 vertices the core and the rest outside. If an outside vertex were unjoined to two other outside vertices, their three core-neighbourhoods would be three sets that Lemma P, a finite fact checked by computer, says cannot exist; so the missing edges among the outside vertices form a matching. Five outside vertices missing only a matching always contain a triangle, so there are at most four, and 35 + 4 = 39; four with no triangle must miss two disjoint edges, which leaves exactly a 4-cycle.

exoo_square.text: Of the 82,251 ways to remove four of the 39 vertices of Exoo’s 1989 graph, exactly one leaves an induced copy of C35(1,7,11,16), and the four removed vertices induce a 4-cycle: the equality case of the theorem appears in Exoo’s example.
exoo_square.caveat: checked on the isomorphism class identified from our own files; Exoo’s pinned bytes were not at home

boxes.smaller_certificate: A smaller certificate for Lemma P: 385 of the 3,360 independent 8-sets suffice, in five orbits of the circulant’s 210 affine symmetries (105 + 70 + 70 + 105 + 35). No union of whole orbits with fewer sets works (1,082 non-empty unions checked). Smaller sub-families exist (an irredundant one of 368 sets), so 385 is minimal only among unions of whole orbits. Confirmed by our own search and by a SAT proof that lrat-check and cake_lpr accept.
boxes.found_by: That Exoo’s graph is C35 plus four vertices in exactly one way was already reported by Unsolved Lab; the full count over all 82,251 four-subsets and the smaller certificate came from a reading by GPT-6.2-astra (via Carlos Toledo’s chat); all of it is checked by our own code.

boxes.second_program: A counter written by the other model family lists the same records. Version 1 ran on all 23,409 cores: on 23,377 it wrote the same screened records as ours, byte for byte by hash. On 32 it wrote more, 14,895 records in all: it applied one of the screen’s three side conditions. Ours applies all three, and our tests refute every one of the 14,895 anyway, so no verdict depends on which program is right. With our correction (version 2) it agrees with ours on those 32 and on 97 other cores tried on a laptop, and on 6,512 of 6,512 cores of a rented run that was stopped on cost after 29 minutes. It was not run on the rest.
boxes.chen: The branch is Zhiyang Chen’s. His notes define it and parked it in October. As we last read his repository (23 November, commit 055ae277), his AI run r310_ralph has a scout note on the same branch, with the same two tests in other words: no assignment survived on 16 pilot inputs, no production run, and an inventory of 23,037 of the 23,409 cores, 372 missing. It says of itself that it changes the status of no case. Ours is a run over all 23,409, with tests that do not assume Case R(7). We have not run his scout.
boxes.corrections_beside: A derivation note in the record says “R(7), not yet closed”: Chen’s run had closed R(7) the day before it was written. The rules say “Timestamped before the pod exists”: the chain shows them only from seven minutes after the run began. Stamped and pinned files cannot change, so both are corrected here.

rest.four_edge: The four-edge branch: its reduction was derived by both model tracks and certified by our reading (the only possible shape is a perfect matching plus one edge; the core then has 76 edges, 216,151 graphs by Table 13). A blind cost pilot was registered and anchored before its beacon, drew 20 of the 216,151 cores, and excluded 20 of 20 (no open, no witness). Its cost, extrapolated to all cores: about US$2,530 as registered, about US$3,111 weighted by the catalogue, about US$510 with four measured optimizations. It was not run: the operator stopped spending on pods that would not close the problem.
